newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Petkim workers stage wage protest.
newsitem.headline: Turk Petkim workers stage wage protest.

text.p: Around 5,500 workers at Turkey's largely state-owned petrochemicals producer Petrokimya Holding A.S. (Petkim) on Monday launched their second protest this month for higher wages, the Petrol-Is union said.
The workers, members of the Petrol-Is union, held a sit-in and stopped goods dispatches at Petkim's Aliaga plant near the Aegean port city of Izmir and Izmit plant near Istanbul.
About 3,300 workers in Aliaga and 2,200 workers at the Izmit plant joined the protest, a union official said. A similar protest was held only in Aliaga for two days from December 3.
The union has been demanding wages to be raised in a scale following a 101 percent increase in the minimum wage in August.
Petrol-Is representative Mustafa Oztaskin repeated their claims that an article in the company's labour contract called for wages of new employees to be raised in tandem with the minimum wage.

The company management had taken the issue to the government earlier this month in reaction to the first protest, but no positive result was obtained although the workers ended their protest after talks with the management.
Oztaskin said the protest would last this time until a solid move was made by the government.
